title: The Inner Instrument
reflection: Today, when your mind feels like a mess, ask which worker is disturbed: manas, buddhi, ahaṁkāra or chitta?

questions.q: What is the antaḥkaraṇa, according to Conversation 2.2?
o: The inner instrument: a system of four workers, which can even pull against each other.
The body’s main nerve, which carries messages between the brain and the heart.
The Self itself, which watches the four workers but takes no part in their work.
A single faculty of the mind, which does all of its work without any help at all.
questions.e: The mind is not one thing. It is a system with four working parts, so you can decide and doubt the same decision at once.
questions.c: The mind is a system of four workers

questions.q: Which worker stamps experience as mine, in Conversation 2.2?
o: Ahaṁkāra, the I-maker: the difference between it is raining and my picnic is ruined.
Manas, the processing mind: the radar that samples, compares and shifts attention.
Buddhi, the decider: the worker that resolves and assigns meaning to what is there.
Chitta, the memory-field: the store of impressions and the deep tendencies of the mind.
questions.e: Manas samples and compares, buddhi decides and assigns meaning, ahaṁkāra makes it mine and chitta stores the impressions and saṁskāras that shape what comes next.

questions.q: A phone buzzes with “can we have a word tomorrow?” and the evening is spoiled. Which worker read it as a threat?
o: Buddhi: change that reading and the whole evening changes.
Manas, which only noticed the buzz and had no part in reading its meaning at all.
Chitta, which acts before any other worker and so sets the reading in advance.
The Self, which reads every message and decides how much it should be feared.
questions.e: Manas detects, buddhi reads it as a threat, ahaṁkāra makes it about me and chitta stores the residue and feeds it forward. The instrument conditions the future by deepening grooves.
questions.c: Buddhi reads the meaning: change it and the evening changes

questions.q: “The inner instrument only processes the present and has no effect on the future.”
questions.e: The instrument does not just process the present: it conditions the future by deepening grooves. Chitta stores the residue and feeds it forward into the next moment.
questions.c: The instrument conditions the future by deepening grooves

questions.q: A man says, “I am anxious,” and then changes it to, “anxiety is here, and I notice it.” What has he done, in Conversation 2.2?
o: Stepped back from the instrument to the awareness that lights it up: the hinge of meditation.
Turned the anxiety into a thought, so that it can be pushed away and then forgotten at once.
Made the anxiety smaller, since a word of this kind lowers its size in each and every case.
Taken the anxiety as his own Self, since it is the thing he is most aware of at just that time.
questions.e: Like a telescope and not the eye, or a violin and not the musician, the four workers process experience but are not the awareness that lights it up. The grammar shift is the hinge of both meditation and modern therapy.
questions.c: The instrument is not the Self

questions.q: A student concludes that the mind is bad and the Self pure, and that they are two things. What does Conversation 2.2 say?
o: Held too hard it makes a cold split: body, mind and Self are one reality at different levels of clarity.
She is right, and the mind must be escaped before the Self can ever be known.
She is right, as long as she does not say so to a person who is suffering.
She is wrong, since the mind and the Self are the very same thing at every level.
questions.e: Vivekananda’s correction: the waves are the ocean moving. The mind is not an enemy to escape; it is to be seen clearly, as the stranger in the mist who turns out to be your friend.
questions.c: Not two things: one reality at different clarity

questions.q: A man decides to change but cannot, though his judgement is clear. Which idea of Conversation 2.2 helps?
o: Slack reins: a clear charioteer cannot steer if attention, manas, was never gathered.
Weak horses: the senses are too strong, and so no charioteer could ever steer them.
A missing rider: the Self has left, and so no one is left to make the decision.
A broken chariot: the body is at fault, and nothing in the mind can be put right.
questions.e: Body is the chariot, senses the horses, manas the reins, buddhi the charioteer and the Self the rider. Just decide to change fails when attention was never gathered.
questions.c: A clear charioteer needs reins: gather attention

questions.q: “Replacing ‘my mind is a mess’ with ‘which worker is disturbed?’ gives a more exact picture of what needs work.”
questions.e: Scattered attention asks for steady manas, poor judgement for clearer buddhi, taking everything personally for softer ahaṁkāra, and old patterns repeating for patient work with chitta. Different ailments, different medicine.
questions.c: Name the worker and the medicine becomes clearer

questions.q: A teacher finds that she takes every comment personally. Which worker does Conversation 2.2 point to, and what is the work?
o: Ahaṁkāra: soften the I-maker that makes each comment about me.
Manas: steady the attention, since she is distracted by all that is said.
Buddhi: improve her judgement, since she misreads the meaning of each remark.
Chitta: clear the memory-field, since the past is the whole of the cause.
questions.e: Taking everything personally is ahaṁkāra at work, and the medicine is softening it. Scattered attention would call for steady manas, and old patterns repeating for patient work with chitta.
questions.c: Taking things personally points to ahaṁkāra

questions.q: How does Conversation 2.2 say science meets this picture halfway?
o: It splits the mind into functions too; the model keeps processing apart from awareness.
It agrees with every point, and so the model needs no further distinction made from it at all.
It rejects the picture, since science finds one function and not four to be at work in the mind.
It has nothing to say, since the inner instrument lies wholly outside what science is able to study.
questions.e: Cognitive science splits the mind into attention, executive control, self-referential processing and memory systems, even memory as a field. The model keeps one extra distinction: processing is not the awareness that illumines it.
questions.c: Science splits the mind too; the model adds awareness
